problem: Calendar note misreads 中旬以後 as days 11–20. Read as 'from the middle decade on', the 4th month gives c.20 May–early June; if the 4th is a slip for the 5th month (c.8 June–7 July), the span runs from about 18 June to 7 July and so includes 4 July. As written, it implies the emended date still falls before the Chinese date.

text_replace.new: The Japanese text says Tengi 2, 4th month, from the middle decade onward (chūjun igo); the 4th month ran from about 10 May to 7 June 1054, so this means roughly 20 May to early June. Read as the 5th month (about 8 June to 7 July), the same wording runs from about 18 June to the month's end and takes in 4 July. The Japanese date is therefore shown as a range and marked approximate.
